children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 4 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex. It's great that he's 4 years old, which means he meets the age requirement (under 16).

Now, could you please tell me if you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

Next, could you tell me about your living arrangements with Alex? Does he live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he does live with me, but his other parent also lives with us and they already claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important detail.

Under the Child Benefit rules, only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child. Since Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you would not be able to make a separate claim for Alex at the same time.

However, if you and the other parent agree that you should be the one to receive the Child Benefit instead, you can arrange to switch who claims it. The current claimant would need to contact the Child Benefit Office to stop their claim, and then you could make a new claim.

If you and the other parent cannot agree on who should claim, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) will make the decision on your behalf.

Would you like me to provide a final summary of your eligibility, or do you have any other questions about this situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, that makes sense. So just to be clear - I'm not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex right now because his other parent is already claiming it, is that right?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's exactly right. Since Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you cannot make a separate claim for Alex at the same time. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child.

If your circumstances change in the future—for example, if the other parent agrees to stop their claim—you would then be able to apply for Child Benefit for Alex yourself.

Let me provide you with a formal summary of your eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Here is a summary of your Child Benefit eligibility:

---

**Child:** Alex (age 4)

**Eligible:** No

**Reason:** Although Alex is under 16 and lives with you in the UK (meeting the basic eligibility criteria), his other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child, so you cannot make a separate claim at this time.

---

**Overall Summary:** You meet many of the requirements for Child Benefit, but because another person is already claiming it for Alex, you are not currently eligible. If you and the other parent agree that you should be the one to claim instead, the other parent would need to stop their claim first, and then you could submit a new application.

If you have any more questions, feel free to ask!
